scenes.headline: How does Nginx *load balance* traffic?
scenes.subtext: Round-robin, least-conn, or IP-hash: which strategy should you use?

scenes.title: Reverse Proxy Traffic Flow
scenes.takeaway: Nginx acts as the front door, distributing incoming HTTP requests across private backends.

scenes.title: Round-Robin vs Least-Conn
scenes.leftDescription: Sends requests sequentially to each backend server in turn. Ideal for uniform, stateless API requests.
scenes.rightDescription: Sends new requests to whichever server currently has the fewest active open connections.
scenes.takeaway: Use Round-Robin for quick web requests; use Least-Connected for heavy tasks or WebSockets.

scenes.title: bash — /etc/nginx/conf.d/lb.conf
scenes.explanation: Declare your upstream cluster and select least_conn or ip_hash in just one directive.

scenes.tagline: Master Linux, Nginx & DevOps step by step
